subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of Porter's five forces is increased when there are many alternative substitute products available?
options: Barriers to exit
The threat of substitutes
Bargaining power of buyers
Bargaining power of suppliers
questions.explain: A wide range of substitutes raises the threat-of-substitutes force, limiting the prices a firm can charge.

questions.q: A horizontal merger occurs when a business combines with another that is:
options: In a completely unrelated industry
At a different stage of the same supply chain
A competitor at the same stage of the same industry
One of its own suppliers
questions.explain: A horizontal merger joins two firms at the same stage of the same industry, often to gain market share and scale.

questions.q: Retrenchment as a strategy involves:
options: Aggressive expansion into new markets
Reducing the scale of operations, e.g. closing divisions or cutting costs
Acquiring a major competitor
Diversifying into unrelated products
questions.explain: Retrenchment is a deliberate cutting-back of the firm's scale, often to restore profitability or focus.

questions.q: In Charles Handy's classification, a 'power culture' is one in which:
options: Control radiates from a central figure or small group with few rules
Individuals work as autonomous experts with little hierarchy
Authority is spread evenly across self-managing teams
Roles and procedures are rigidly defined by bureaucracy
questions.explain: A power culture centres control on a dominant individual or core group, with decisions made centrally and few formal rules.

questions.q: According to Ansoff's matrix, the strategy of launching a new product into a new market is:
options: Diversification, the highest risk
Market penetration, the lowest risk
Market development, a moderate risk
Product development, a moderate risk
questions.explain: Diversification means new product plus new market and is the riskiest quadrant of Ansoff's matrix.

questions.q: Which statement best captures the difference between strategy and tactics?
options: Strategy sets long-term direction to achieve overall objectives; tactics are the shorter-term actions used to implement it
Tactics are decided by senior managers; strategy is decided by junior staff
Strategy is short-term and reactive; tactics are long-term and planned
Strategy and tactics are interchangeable terms for the same plans
questions.explain: Strategy is the long-term plan for achieving objectives, while tactics are the day-to-day or short-term actions that carry the strategy out.

questions.q: Managing risk through a risk assessment typically involves identifying hazards and then:
options: Ignoring low-probability events entirely
Eliminating all risk so that none remains
Transferring every risk to employees
Assessing the likelihood and impact of each risk and planning mitigation
questions.explain: Risk management evaluates each risk's probability and impact and then decides how to reduce, transfer or accept it.

questions.q: Organisational culture can act as a barrier to change because:
options: Deeply held values and 'the way we do things here' may conflict with new methods
It has no influence on employee behaviour
It only affects junior staff, never managers
Cultures change instantly when leaders demand it
questions.explain: An entrenched culture embodies shared assumptions that can clash with and resist new strategies.

questions.q: Contingency planning is best described as:
options: A plan for everyday routine operations
A method of calculating depreciation
A long-term marketing strategy
A set of plans prepared in advance for specific possible crises or emergencies
questions.explain: Contingency planning prepares what-if responses to specific possible events such as fires, IT failures or supplier collapse.

questions.q: Scenario planning is mainly used to help a business:
options: Calculate the exact break-even output
Set fixed annual sales targets with certainty
Record last year's financial results accurately
Prepare for a range of possible future situations and uncertainties
questions.explain: Scenario planning explores several plausible futures so the firm can prepare responses to uncertain conditions.

questions.q: A SWOT analysis would classify a new free-trade agreement opening up an export market as a:
options: Strength
Weakness
Threat
Opportunity
questions.explain: A favourable external development such as a new export market is an opportunity in SWOT.

questions.q: Handy's 'role culture' is typically associated with:
options: A flexible, project-based structure
A bureaucratic organisation with clear job roles, rules and hierarchy
An entrepreneur making all decisions personally
A loose network of independent specialists
questions.explain: A role culture is bureaucratic, relying on defined roles, procedures and a clear hierarchy.

questions.q: A joint venture differs from a takeover because in a joint venture:
options: No resources are ever pooled
Two or more firms set up and share a new, separate enterprise
It is always between firms in unrelated industries
One firm gains full ownership and control of the other
questions.explain: In a joint venture, partner firms share ownership, risk and resources in a jointly created enterprise rather than one absorbing the other.

questions.q: Kotter and Schlesinger suggest that 'manipulation and co-optation' as a way of handling resistance is:
options: Only suitable when there is no time pressure
Identical to participation and involvement
A fast approach that can lead to future problems if people feel manipulated
The slowest but most ethical approach
questions.explain: Manipulation and co-optation can be quick and cheap but risks resentment and loss of trust if discovered.

questions.q: In Porter's five forces, a high threat of new entrants is most likely when:
options: Customers face large switching costs to change supplier
Barriers to entry such as high capital costs and brand loyalty are low
Capital requirements to enter the market are very high
Existing firms hold strong patents and economies of scale
questions.explain: Low barriers to entry make it easy for new competitors to enter, raising the threat of new entrants.

questions.q: Offshoring differs from outsourcing because offshoring specifically means:
options: Selling a subsidiary to a foreign buyer
Using a third party in the same country
Relocating a business activity to another country (whether kept in-house or not)
Importing finished goods from abroad
questions.explain: Offshoring is relocating an activity abroad; it can be done in-house and is therefore distinct from outsourcing.

questions.q: In a SWOT analysis, which pairing correctly classifies the factors as internal or external?
options: Strengths and opportunities are internal; weaknesses and threats are external
All four factors are internal to the business
Strengths and weaknesses are internal; opportunities and threats are external
Opportunities and weaknesses are internal; strengths and threats are external
questions.explain: SWOT separates internal strengths and weaknesses from external opportunities and threats.

questions.q: In the Boston Matrix (portfolio analysis), a 'cash cow' is a product with:
options: Low market share in a low-growth market
High market share in a low-growth market
Low market share in a high-growth market
High market share in a high-growth market
questions.explain: A cash cow has high share of a low-growth market, generating steady cash with little investment.

questions.q: In Porter's value chain, which of the following is a primary activity rather than a support activity?
options: Technology development
Firm infrastructure
Outbound logistics
Human resource management
questions.explain: Outbound logistics is one of the five primary activities; HRM, technology development and infrastructure are support activities.

questions.q: In Kotter and Schlesinger's framework, which is one of the recognised methods of overcoming resistance to change?
options: Removing all managers from the process
Ignoring affected employees entirely
Refusing to negotiate under any circumstances
Education and communication
questions.explain: Education and communication is one of Kotter and Schlesinger's six approaches to managing resistance to change.

questions.q: A core competence, according to Hamel and Prahalad, is best described as:
options: Any activity the business performs, however ordinary
The cheapest production process a firm uses
A distinctive capability that is hard to imitate and gives access to many markets
A short-term marketing campaign
questions.explain: A core competence is a hard-to-imitate strength that provides competitive advantage and potential entry to multiple markets.

questions.q: Buyer (customer) bargaining power in Porter's model tends to be highest when:
options: There are many small buyers and products are highly differentiated
The product is essential and has no alternatives
Switching costs for buyers are extremely high
There are few buyers each purchasing large volumes and products are undifferentiated
questions.explain: A small number of large buyers facing standardised products can demand lower prices, giving them strong bargaining power.

questions.q: A strategic alliance differs from a full merger because the partners:
options: Are always in unrelated industries
Cannot share any technology or resources
Cooperate on specific activities while remaining independent businesses
Lose their separate identities completely
questions.explain: In a strategic alliance, firms cooperate on agreed areas yet stay independent, unlike a merger where they combine into one.

questions.q: A key advantage of inorganic growth by takeover compared with organic growth is that it:
options: Never requires significant financing
Can achieve rapid expansion and instant market share
Guarantees lower costs immediately
Always avoids any culture clash between firms
questions.explain: Takeovers allow fast growth and an immediate gain in market share, though they carry risks such as culture clashes.

questions.q: Organic (internal) growth is best described as:
options: A deliberate reduction in the scale of operations
Growth achieved only through joint ventures
Growth generated from within the firm, such as by selling more or opening new outlets
Growth through acquiring or merging with other businesses
questions.explain: Organic growth comes from expanding the firm's own operations rather than buying other firms.

questions.q: A common cause of resistance to change among employees is:
options: A strong desire for more uncertainty
An eagerness to lose established routines
Excessive confidence that change will benefit them
Fear of the unknown and concern over job security
questions.explain: People often resist change because of fear of the unknown and worries about their jobs and status.

questions.q: A firm sells its existing products to a new overseas market for the first time. On Ansoff's matrix this is:
options: Diversification
Product development
Market development
Market penetration
questions.explain: Selling existing products to new markets is market development.

questions.q: On Ansoff's matrix, which cell combines an existing product with an existing market?
options: Market penetration
Product development
Diversification
Market development
questions.explain: Market penetration uses existing products in existing markets and is the lowest-risk option.

questions.q: Outsourcing is best defined as:
options: Buying out a supplier to control it directly
Paying an external provider to carry out activities previously done in-house
Relocating part of a firm's own operations to another country
Merging with a foreign competitor
questions.explain: Outsourcing means contracting an outside organisation to perform tasks the business used to do itself.

questions.q: In the Boston Matrix, a 'problem child' (question mark) is characterised by:
options: High market share, high market growth
Low market share, high market growth
High market share, low market growth
Low market share, low market growth
questions.explain: Problem children have low share in fast-growing markets and need heavy investment to develop.
